boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus places for studying, gathering, making art, and joining public-facing college activities.

cards.title: Set up at Davis Family Library
cards.subtitle: Main campus library
cards.notes: Use the communal workspaces, group-study rooms, and reading chairs for a collaborative session; reserve a study space through the library when needed.
cards.short_summary: The main library combines shared work areas with research and academic-support services.
cards.evidence_claim: Middlebury identifies Davis as its main campus library with communal workspaces on all three levels, group-study rooms, and a study-space reservation system.
cards.access_notes: Library access and reservable-space availability can vary; use the library reservation system for bookable rooms.

cards.title: Meet up at McCullough
cards.subtitle: Student center on the Main Quadrangle
cards.notes: Choose McCullough for a group meeting, event, meal stop, or performance; its rooms and social space support student organizations and campus programming.
cards.short_summary: A student-center hub with meeting rooms, food services, event space, and the Office of Student Engagement.
cards.evidence_claim: Middlebury says McCullough provides events, programming and meeting space, food services, and a social space reservable by student organizations and college departments.
cards.access_notes: Meeting and social spaces may require a reservation; check event or building access before visiting.

cards.title: Take a study break at the museum
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to Mahaney Arts Center
cards.notes: Walk through the galleries between classes, then look for gallery talks, films, lectures, or workshops listed by the museum and arts program.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum with ancient-to-contemporary collections and programs that connect art with courses.
cards.evidence_claim: Middlebury describes the museum as a relaxing study-break destination with several thousand objects and regular lectures, gallery talks, films, and workshops; admission and programs are free to all.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current gallery and program schedules before visiting.

cards.title: Find an arts event at the MAC
cards.subtitle: Kevin P. Mahaney ’84 Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Check the arts calendar, then head to the MAC for exhibitions or performances in its concert hall, theatre, and dance spaces.
cards.short_summary: The MAC is a campus arts hub that brings performance, exhibition, and academic arts programs together.
cards.evidence_claim: Middlebury identifies the Mahaney Arts Center as a campus arts hub housing the Museum of Art, Seeler Studio Theatre, dance theatre, and Robison Hall.
cards.access_notes: Performance and gallery access depends on the event schedule; confirm ticketing or entry details in advance.

cards.title: Listen for the carillon at Mead Chapel
cards.subtitle: Chapel Row landmark
cards.notes: Pause outside to hear the daily carillon, or check campus arts listings for concerts, lectures, and other major events held in the chapel.
cards.short_summary: A central campus landmark used for choral music, lectures, concerts, and major college events.
cards.evidence_claim: Middlebury states that Mead Chapel hosts College Choir and Collegium Ensemble performances, lectures, Performing Arts Series concerts, major public events, and a carillon played daily.
cards.access_notes: Interior access and event attendance vary; consult the relevant campus event listing.

cards.title: Get your hands in the soil at The Knoll
cards.subtitle: Middlebury’s student-powered garden
cards.notes: Look for volunteer hours or garden opportunities through Sustainability and Environmental Affairs, then join a hands-on session with other campus participants.
cards.short_summary: A student-powered garden where students can garden, do research, and connect with community.
cards.evidence_claim: Middlebury describes The Knoll as a student-powered garden offering opportunities for soil work, research, and community connection.
cards.access_notes: Check the listed Knoll Garden volunteer hours or contact Sustainability and Environmental Affairs before participating.

cards.title: Connect sustainability work at Hillcrest
cards.subtitle: 531 College Street
cards.notes: Use Hillcrest as a starting point for environmental studies and sustainability programming; contact the listed office for current co-curricular opportunities.
cards.short_summary: A LEED Platinum environmental center housing Environmental Studies and Sustainability and Environmental Affairs.
cards.evidence_claim: Middlebury says Hillcrest houses the Environmental Studies program and Sustainability and Environmental Affairs, which coordinates co-curricular programming and sustainability integration.
cards.source_title: Franklin Environmental Center at Hillcrest | Middlebury
cards.access_notes: Office and program access may vary; contact the center or review current program information before visiting.

cards.title: Watch for a Mittelman stargazing event
cards.subtitle: McCardell Bicentennial Hall
cards.notes: Follow the observatory events page for the next stargazing session and its weather update; arrive only for a listed event or arranged academic activity.
cards.short_summary: An observatory supporting astronomy coursework, research, educational outreach, and campus-community stargazing events.
cards.evidence_claim: Middlebury says Mittelman Observatory supports astronomy coursework, research, and educational outreach, and welcomes campus and local-community guests for stargazing events.
cards.access_notes: Stargazing is weather-dependent; check the observatory events page for scheduled sessions and same-day status.

cards.title: Take the Main Quadrangle route
cards.subtitle: Central campus green
cards.notes: Use this broad green as a simple outdoor meeting point between Old Stone Row, Chapel Row, and McCullough; keep to open, publicly used paths.
cards.short_summary: The historic central quadrangle links several of Middlebury’s most recognizable campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Middlebury Libraries describes Athletic Fields as the large green quadrangle at the core of campus, defined by Chapel Row, Old Stone Row, and McCullough Student Center.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor campus landscape; respect posted event setups, maintenance areas, and access guidance.

cards.title: Orient yourself at Old Chapel
cards.subtitle: Old Chapel Road
cards.notes: Use this Old Stone Row landmark to get oriented before exploring nearby academic and student-life destinations; enjoy it from the exterior unless access is posted.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus building that once held a chapel, library, museum, classrooms, and lecture halls.
cards.evidence_claim: Middlebury’s campus guide states that Old Chapel was built in 1836 as the center of student life and originally contained the campus library, mineralogy museum, classrooms, lecture halls, offices, and chapel.
cards.source_title: Campus Map and Guide | Middlebury College
cards.access_notes: Administrative offices occupy the building; view the exterior and follow posted access guidance.
